chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Zayd al-Zarrād, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh (عليه السلام), who said:

Rasūl Allāh (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) said: “Indeed, great affliction is met with great recompense. So when Allah loves a servant, He afflicts him with great affliction. Thus, whoever is pleased, for him with Allah is pleasure; and whoever is angered by the affliction, for him with Allah is wrath.”

key_terms.أَحَبَّ اللَّهُ: Allah loved; indicating divine favor toward the servant
key_terms.رَضِيَ: was pleased and accepted the trial with contentment
key_terms.عَظِيمَ الْبَلَاءِ: severe affliction or great trial endured by a servant
key_terms.عَظِيمُ الْجَزَاءِ: great recompense and reward from Allah

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah test those whom He loves with severe afflictions?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that severe trials can be a sign of divine love and are accompanied by immense reward. It emphasizes the spiritual importance of riḍā with Allah’s decree, while warning that resentment toward affliction leads to divine displeasure.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Zayd Al Zarrad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The great affliction is matched with great Recompense. So when Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Loves a servant, Afflicts him with the great affliction. So the one who is pleased, for him would be the Pleasure in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the one who is angered by the affliction, for him would be the Anger in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 8. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Zayd al-Zarrad from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘

The great misfortunes are matched with great rewards. When Allah loves a servant He tries him with great misfortunes. Whoever accepts it, Allah accepts him and whoever becomes angry with misfortunes, with Allah for him there is anger.”’
